name: navigation friction
description: Users have difficulty moving through Netflix, locating content or controls, returning to a previous screen, or navigating efficiently with a remote or touch interface.
aliases: navigation issue|hard to navigate|menu confusion|cannot find|difficult to return|back navigation|too much scrolling|lost in rows|remote navigation|navigation difficulty
examples: I had to move through several rows before finding the section I wanted. I could not easily return to the episode after leaving playback. The TV navigation took more effort than expected.

name: interaction friction
description: Controls or input methods make actions difficult, imprecise, or error-prone, including accidental taps, remote-control mistakes, and closely spaced controls.
aliases: interaction issue|control friction|accidental tap|accidental input|remote mistake|imprecise control|small control|closely spaced controls|touch friction|input difficulty
examples: I tapped the wrong playback control on my phone. A small remote movement changed the selected item. I accidentally exited because the controls were too easy to trigger.

name: inefficient workflow
description: A viewing goal can be completed, but it requires unnecessary steps, repeated checking, excessive browsing, or avoidable effort.
aliases: too many steps|extra steps|slow process|repeated checking|too much effort|inefficient browsing|tedious workflow|takes too long|unnecessary navigation|cumbersome process
examples: I had to check the profile, search again, and reopen the title before watching. Finding a suitable option required too much scrolling. The task worked, but it took more steps than it should have.

name: high cognitive load
description: The interface presents too many options, dense information, or unclear distinctions, requiring excessive mental effort to compare titles or make a viewing decision.
aliases: choice overload|too many options|mental effort|decision burden|overwhelming rows|hard to compare|too much information|dense interface|cognitive overload|difficult decision
examples: There were so many similar rows that choosing became tiring. I had to compare too many titles before deciding. The screen demanded more attention than I wanted to give it.

name: visual clutter
description: Dense rows, crowded artwork, competing visual elements, or weak hierarchy make the interface tiring or difficult to scan.
aliases: crowded interface|visual density|busy rows|too many thumbnails|weak hierarchy|cluttered screen|dense rows|hard to scan|crowded layout|visual overload
examples: The rows felt visually crowded on the TV. Similar-looking artwork made titles difficult to distinguish. The screen was too busy to scan comfortably.

name: search quality
description: Search results are irrelevant, overly broad, poorly matched, incomplete, or otherwise fail to help users find the requested content.
aliases: poor search|irrelevant results|generic results|search mismatch|bad search results|cannot find title|weak search|search failure|results not relevant|search accuracy
examples: I searched for a specific type of action film, but the results were too generic. The title I expected did not appear clearly. Search returned options that did not match what I asked for.

name: search refinement
description: Search lacks useful filters or refinement options for narrowing results by language, region, genre, director, film type, or other meaningful attributes.
aliases: search filters|filter search|refine results|advanced search|narrow results|language filter|genre filter|director search|manual filtering|search precision
examples: I could not narrow the results by language or region. I had to manually inspect many titles because there were no useful filters. Search needed more precise refinement options.

name: poor recovery
description: After an accidental exit, interruption, playback problem, or unwanted state, users cannot easily return to the correct title, episode, or playback position.
aliases: recovery problem|cannot resume|lost place|wrong playback position|restart required|accidental exit|hard to return|resume failure|lost progress|playback recovery
examples: After exiting by mistake, I struggled to return to the same episode. The film restarted from the wrong point. Recovering from the interruption took several attempts.

name: insufficient action feedback
description: Netflix does not provide clear or timely visual confirmation after an action, leaving users uncertain whether a selection, setting, or transition was applied.
aliases: feedback problem|no feedback|missing confirmation|unclear response|action not confirmed|selection unclear|delayed feedback|silent action|no visual response|confirmation problem
examples: I changed the subtitle setting but was not sure it had applied. The selection changed without a clear confirmation. I repeated the action because the interface did not respond clearly.

name: unclear system state
description: Users cannot determine the current playback, loading, selection, or application state from the information shown on screen.
aliases: system state unclear|unknown state|playback state unclear|loading unclear|not sure what happened|status unclear|current state|state change missed|active state unclear|system status
examples: I could not tell whether playback was paused or loading. I missed the state change after pressing the remote. The interface did not make the current status obvious.

name: profile confusion
description: Users enter, browse, or watch from the wrong profile, or have difficulty separating household members’ viewing histories and recommendations.
aliases: wrong profile|profile mix-up|mixed profiles|profile switching issue|household profile confusion|recommendations mixed|incorrect profile|profile separation|shared account confusion|profile-related confusion
examples: I started watching from the wrong profile. The recommendations looked like someone else’s viewing history. I had to switch profiles before continuing.

name: unclear profile state
description: The active Netflix profile is not sufficiently visible or distinguishable, so users must check which profile is currently selected.
aliases: profile state unclear|active profile unclear|which profile|profile indicator|profile awareness|current profile|profile not obvious|profile identification|selected profile unclear|profile visibility
examples: I had to stop and check which profile was active. The TV did not make the selected profile obvious. I only noticed the wrong profile after seeing unfamiliar recommendations.

name: trust in personalization
description: Users doubt whether recommendations accurately reflect their preferences, viewing history, profile, mood, or stated interests.
aliases: personalization trust|recommendation trust|does not know me|poor personalization|mixed recommendations|generic recommendations|recommendation relevance|preferences ignored|personalization doubt|recommendations not tailored
examples: The recommendations did not feel specific to my interests. I was unsure why these titles were being suggested. The rows felt generic rather than personalized.

name: content freshness
description: Recommended or promoted content feels repetitive, outdated, insufficiently current, or disconnected from what users perceive as new or trending.
aliases: stale content|not current|repetitive recommendations|same titles|outdated rows|fresh content|trending content missing|content feels old|lack of novelty|repeated suggestions
examples: The trending rows did not feel current. I kept seeing the same titles across several sessions. The recommendations needed fresher options.

name: clarity of categories
description: Category names, grouping logic, or boundaries are vague, overlapping, overly broad, or insufficiently meaningful for discovery.
aliases: category clarity|unclear categories|overlapping categories|generic categories|category labels|poor categorization|broad categories|category logic|row labels unclear|content grouping
examples: Several categories seemed to contain the same kinds of titles. The row labels were too broad to guide my choice. I could not understand how the content had been grouped.

name: cross-device continuity
description: Users experience friction when moving browsing or viewing activity between phone, tablet, laptop, and Smart TV.
aliases: device switching|cross-device issue|phone to TV|laptop to TV|handoff problem|switch devices|device transition|continue on another device|cross-device experience|device continuity
examples: I found the title on my phone but had to look for it again on the TV. Moving from laptop to TV required extra checking. The handoff between devices did not feel seamless.

name: continuity of progress
description: Viewing progress, playback position, recently watched status, or session history does not carry over clearly or reliably across sessions or devices.
aliases: progress continuity|watch progress|playback position|resume position|continue watching issue|progress not synced|lost progress|recent activity missing|session continuity|watch history continuity
examples: The episode did not resume where I left it. My progress was not obvious after switching devices. I had to find the correct point again.

name: clarity of watched state
description: Users cannot easily tell whether a title or episode has already been watched, partially watched, or remains unwatched.
aliases: watched state|episode status|already watched|unwatched unclear|viewing status|progress indicator unclear|watched indicator|episode completion|seen or unseen|watch history state
examples: I could not tell whether I had already watched the episode. The progress marker was too subtle. I had to open the title to confirm where I was.

name: subtitle or audio support problem
description: Subtitle, caption, language, or audio settings are difficult to find, enable, read, confirm, or maintain during viewing.
aliases: subtitle problem|captions issue|audio support|subtitles missing|subtitle settings|caption readability|audio language|subtitles not enabled|hearing support|language settings
examples: I was not sure whether subtitles were enabled. The subtitle text was too small to read comfortably. I had to adjust the language settings again before watching.

name: accessibility barrier
description: The interface creates difficulty for users with visual, hearing, motor, or other accessibility needs, reducing their ability to browse, understand, or control Netflix independently.
aliases: accessibility issue|a11y barrier|low vision|hard of hearing|color blindness|motor difficulty|visual accessibility|hearing accessibility|accessible controls|disability barrier
examples: Low-contrast labels were difficult to read. Small controls were hard to use with a hand tremor. Missing or unclear subtitles made dialogue difficult to follow.

name: low contrast
description: Text, labels, controls, selected states, or other visual cues do not have enough contrast to be perceived comfortably.
aliases: contrast issue|faint text|low-contrast label|hard to see|weak contrast|color contrast|subtle state|washed out text|poor visibility|contrast sensitivity
examples: The secondary text was too faint on the TV. Selected and unselected controls looked too similar. I struggled to distinguish the label in low light.

name: content readability issue
description: Titles, descriptions, labels, subtitles, or secondary text are too small, dense, or otherwise difficult to read at the user’s viewing distance or device size.
aliases: small text|hard to read|text readability|tiny labels|description difficult|subtitle size|reading difficulty|secondary text|visual readability|text too small
examples: The description text was difficult to read from the sofa. The subtitle size was too small on the phone. I had to move closer to read the secondary information.

name: color-dependent visual cues
description: Important interface states or distinctions rely mainly on color, making them difficult to interpret for users with color-vision differences.
aliases: color-only cue|color dependent|color blindness issue|state by color|selected state color|visual cue unclear|color distinction|color-coded status|colour cue|color accessibility
examples: I could not distinguish the selected control because the state changed mainly by color. Two status indicators looked the same to me. The current option needed a non-color cue.

name: choice overload
description: The number or similarity of available titles makes choosing difficult, leading to prolonged browsing, indecision, or abandonment.
aliases: too many choices|browsing overload|decision paralysis|cannot decide|endless browsing|too many titles|option overload|choice paralysis|gave up browsing|selection overload
examples: I kept scrolling because there were too many similar options. I gave up without choosing anything. The number of titles made a quick decision harder.
